title: The Desert Showdown and the First Crew
paragraphs: Next, the Spirit led Jesus deep into the wilderness to be tested by the devil. The devil was ready for it. Jesus went without food for forty days and forty nights. He was starving. Then the devil moved in: “Since you're really God's Son, say the word and turn these stones into loaves of bread.”
§ Strike 1
Jesus shut him down with a quote from Deuteronomy: “People need more than bread to survive; they need a steady stream of words coming from God's mouth.”
§ Strike 2

For the second test the devil took him to the Holy City — the highest point of the Temple. “Since you're God's Son, jump,” the devil said, and he goaded Jesus by quoting Psalm 91: “He has placed you in the care of angels. They will catch you so that you won't so much as stub your toe on a stone.”
Jesus countered with another quote from Deuteronomy: “Don't you dare test the Lord your God.”
§ Strike 3

For the third test, the devil took him to the peak of a huge mountain. He gestured expansively, pointing out all the earth's kingdoms and how glorious they all were. “They're yours — lock, stock, and barrel,” the devil said. “Just go down on your knees and worship me, and they're yours.”

Jesus' refusal was short and sharp: “Beat it, Satan!” Then he backed his rebuke with a third quote from Deuteronomy: “Worship the Lord your God, and only him. Serve him with absolute single-heartedness.”
The devil lost, packed up, and left. Angels came and took care of Jesus.

When Jesus heard that John had been arrested, he headed back to Galilee. He moved from his hometown Nazareth to the lakeside village of Capernaum, nestled at the base of the Zebulun and Naphtali hills. This move brought Isaiah's prophecy to life: “Land of Zebulun, land of Naphtali, road to the sea, over Jordan, Galilee, crossroads for the nations. People sitting out their lives in the dark saw a huge light; sitting in that dark, dark country of death, they watched the sun come up.” This Isaiah-prophesied revelation came to life in Galilee the moment Jesus started preaching. He picked up right where John left off: “Change your life. God's kingdom is here.”
§ Building the Team

Walking along the beach of Lake Galilee, Jesus saw two brothers — Simon (later called Peter) and Andrew — fishing, throwing their nets into the lake. It was their regular work. Jesus said to them, “Come with me. I'll make a new kind of fisherman out of you. I'll show you how to catch men and women instead of perch and bass.” They didn't ask questions, but simply dropped their nets and followed.

A short distance down the beach, they came upon another pair of brothers — James and John, Zebedee's sons. These two were sitting in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their fishnets. Jesus made them the same offer, and they were just as quick to follow, abandoning the boat and their father.

From there he went all over Galilee. He used synagogues as meeting places and taught people the truth of God. God's kingdom was his theme — that starting right now, they were under God's government, a good government! He also healed people of their diseases and the bad effects of their bad lives. Word got around the entire Roman province of Syria. People brought anyone with a sickness — whether mental, emotional, or physical. Jesus healed them, one and all. More and more people came, the momentum building. Besides people from Galilee, crowds came from the “Ten Towns” across the lake, others up from Jerusalem and Judea, still others from across the Jordan.

title: The Sermon on the Mount (The Rulebook Flip)
paragraphs: Seeing the massive crowd, Jesus hiked up a hill, and those who were apprenticed to him — the committed — climbed with him. Arriving at a quiet place, he sat down and taught his climbing companions. This is what he said:
§ The Beatitudes
"You're blessed when you're at the end of your rope. With less of you, there is more of God and his rule."
"You're blessed when you feel you've lost what is most dear to you. Only then can you be embraced by the One most dear to you."
"You're blessed when you're content with just who you are—no more, no less. That's the moment you find yourselves proud owners of everything that can't be bought."
"You're blessed when you've worked up a good appetite for God. He's food and drink in the best meal you'll ever eat."
"You're blessed when you care. At the moment of being 'care-full,' you find yourselves cared for."
"You're blessed when you get your inside world—your mind and heart—put right. Then you can see God in the outside world."
"You're blessed when you can show people how to cooperate instead of compete or fight. That's when you discover who you really are, and your place in God's family."
"You're blessed when your commitment to God provokes persecution. The persecution drives you even deeper into God's kingdom."

"Not only that—count yourselves blessed every time people put you down or throw you out or speak lies about you to discredit me. What it means is that the truth is too close for comfort and they are uncomfortable. You can be glad when that happens—give a cheer, even!—for though they don't like it, I do! And all heaven applauds. You are in good company. My prophets and witnesses have always gotten into this kind of trouble."
§ Salt and Light

"Let me tell you why you are here. You're here to be salt-seasoning that brings out the God-flavors of this earth. If you lose your saltiness, how will people taste godliness? You've lost your usefulness and will end up in the garbage."

"Here's another way to put it: You're here to be light, bringing out the God-colors in the world. God is not a secret to be kept. We're going public with this, as public as a city on a hill. If I make you light-bearers, you don't think I'm going to hide you under a bucket, do you? I'm putting you on a light stand. Now that I've put you there on a hilltop, on a light stand—shine! Keep open house; be generous with your lives. By opening up to others, you'll prompt people to open up with God, this generous Father in heaven."
§ Completing God's Law

"Don't suppose for a minute that I have come to demolish the Scriptures—either God's Law or the Prophets. I'm not here to demolish but to complete. I am going to put it all together, pull it all together in a vast panorama. God's Law is more real and lasting than the stars in the sky and the ground at your feet. Long after stars burn out and earth wears out, God's Law will be alive and working."

"Trivialize even the smallest item in God's Law and you will only have trivialized yourself. But take it seriously, show the way for others, and you will find honor in the kingdom. Unless you do far better than the Pharisees in the matters of right living, you won't know the first thing about entering the kingdom."
§ On Anger

"You're familiar with the command to the ancients, 'Do not murder.' I'm telling you that anyone who is so much as angry with a brother or sister is guilty of murder. Carelessly call a brother 'idiot!' and you just might find yourself hauled into court. Thoughtlessly yell 'stupid!' at a sister and you are on the brink of hellfire. The simple moral fact is that words kill."

"This is how I want you to conduct yourself in these matters. If you enter your place of worship and, about to make an offering, you suddenly remember a grudge a friend has against you, abandon your offering, leave immediately, go to this friend and make things right. Then and only then, come back and work things out with God."

Or say you're out on the street and an old enemy accosts you. Don't lose a minute. Make the first move; make things right with him. After all, if you leave the first move to him, knowing his track record, you're likely to end up in court, maybe even jail. If that happens, you won't get out without a stiff fine.
§ On Lust

"You know the next commandment pretty well, too: 'Don't go to bed with another's spouse.' But don't think you've preserved your virtue simply by staying out of bed. Your heart can be corrupted by lust even quicker than your body. Those ogling looks you think nobody notices—they also corrupt."

"Let's not pretend this is easier than it really is. If you want to live a morally pure life, here's what you have to do: You have to blind your right eye the moment you catch it in a lustful leer. You have to choose to live one-eyed or else be dumped on a moral trash pile. And you have to chop off your right hand the moment you notice it raised threateningly. Better a bloody stump than your entire being discarded for good in the dump."
§ On Divorce

"Remember the Scripture that says, 'Whoever divorces his wife, let him do it legally, giving her divorce papers and her legal rights'? Too many of you are using that as a cover for selfishness and whim, pretending to be righteous just because you are 'legal.' Please, no more pretending. If you divorce your wife, you're responsible for making her an adulteress (unless she has already made herself that by sexual promiscuity). And if you marry such a divorced adulteress, you're automatically an adulterer yourself. You can't use legal cover to mask a moral failure."
§ On Oaths

"And don't say anything you don't mean. This counsel is embedded deep in our traditions. You only make things worse when you lay down a smoke screen of pious talk, saying, 'I'll pray for you,' and never doing it, or saying, 'God be with you,' and not meaning it. You don't make your words true by embellishing them with religious lace. In making your speech sound more religious, it becomes less true. Just say 'yes' and 'no.' When you manipulate words to get your own way, you go wrong."
§ On Revenge

"Here's another old saying that deserves a second look: 'Eye for eye, tooth for tooth.' Is that going to get us anywhere? Here's what I propose: 'Don't hit back at all.' If someone strikes you, stand there and take it. If someone drags you into court and sues for the shirt off your back, giftwrap your best coat and make a present of it. And if someone takes unfair advantage of you, use the occasion to practice the servant life. No more tit-for-tat stuff. Live generously."
§ On Enemies

"You're familiar with the old written law, 'Love your friend,' and its unwritten companion, 'Hate your enemy.' I'm challenging that. I'm telling you to love your enemies. Let them bring out the best in you, not the worst. When someone gives you a hard time, respond with the supple, flexible moves of prayer, for then you are working out of your true selves, your God-created selves."

"This is what God does. He gives his best—the sun to warm and the rain to nourish—to everyone, regardless: the good and bad, the nice and nasty. If all you do is love the lovable, do you expect a bonus? Anybody can do that. If you simply say hello to those who greet you, do you expect a medal? Any run-of-the-mill sinner does that."
"In a word, what I'm saying is, Grow up. You're kingdom subjects. Now live like it. Live out your God-created identity. Live generously and graciously toward others, the way God lives toward you."

title: How to Actually Live It Out (Sermon on the Mount, Part 2)
paragraphs: Okay, pay super close attention when you're trying to do good deeds. Make sure you're not just putting on a show for everyone. It might look impressive, like a great performance, but God, who totally created you, won't be clapping for that.

When you're helping someone out, don't try to make a big deal about it or draw attention to yourself. I bet you've seen people like this – I call them 'playactors.' They treat everything like a stage, whether it's a prayer meeting or just hanging out on a street corner, acting all caring only when people are watching, totally playing to the crowd.

Sure, they get some cheers and likes, but honestly, that's all they'll get. When you're helping someone, don't even think about how it'll look to others. Just do it – keep it chill, keep it quiet, don't make a scene. That's exactly how your God, who imagined you and loves you deeply, works behind the scenes to help you out.
§ Praying Simply

And when you're talking to God, don't turn that into some dramatic performance either. All these people making a regular show out of their prayers, hoping for fifteen minutes of fame! Do you really think God is sitting there in a special box seat watching your act?

Here’s what I want you to do instead: Find a quiet, private spot so you won't even be tempted to put on a role-play in front of God. Just be yourself there, as simply and honestly as you possibly can.
The focus will shift from you to God, and you'll start to really feel his grace.

The world is full of so-called prayer warriors who actually know nothing about prayer. They're all about formulas, programs, and advice, trying to sell you techniques for how to get whatever you want from God. Don't fall for that nonsense.
This is your Father you're dealing with, and he knows way better than you do what you actually need. With a God like this, who loves you so much, you can pray super simply. Like this:

"Our Father in heaven, reveal who you really are. Set the world right; do what’s best – here on Earth, just like it is in heaven. Keep us alive with enough food to eat every day. Keep us forgiven by you and help us forgive others. Keep us safe from ourselves and from the Devil. You’re totally in charge! You can do anything you want! You’re amazing and beautiful! Yes. Yes. Yes."
In prayer, there’s a real connection between what God does and what you do. For example, you can't expect to get forgiveness from God without also forgiving other people.
If you refuse to do your part, you basically cut yourself off from what God wants to do for you.

When you choose to skip some meals or give up something you like to focus better on God (that's called an appetite-denying discipline or fasting), don't make a big deal out of it. You might become a minor celebrity for a bit, but it won’t make you a saint.

If you're 'training' inwardly (working on your spiritual life), just act normal outwardly. Go ahead and shampoo your hair, comb it, brush your teeth, wash your face. God doesn't need you to put on a show to get his attention.
He won't miss what you're doing; he'll totally reward you well.
§ A Life Focused on God

Don’t hoard up treasures down here on Earth where moths can eat them, rust can corrode them, or – even worse! – burglars can break in and steal them. Instead, stockpile your treasures in heaven, where they’re totally safe from moths, rust, and burglars.
It's pretty obvious, right? The place where your treasure is, is the place you'll most want to be, and that's where you'll end up being.

Your eyes are like windows into your body. If you open your eyes wide with wonder and belief, your whole body fills up with light. But if you live with squinty eyes, full of greed and distrust, your body is like a musty, dark basement.
If you pull the blinds down on your windows (meaning you choose to live in darkness), what a super dark life you will have!

You seriously can't worship two gods at the same time. If you love one god, you'll end up hating the other. Adoring one will make you feel contempt for the other. You absolutely can't worship God and Money both.

If you decide to live for God, focusing your life on worshipping him, then it naturally follows that you won't fuss about what's on the table for dinner or whether your clothes in the closet are super trendy.

There's so much more to your life than the food you put in your stomach, and way more to your outer appearance than the clothes you wear. Look at the birds, they're free and not tied down to a job or worried about anything; God takes care of them.
And you matter way more to him than birds do.
Has anyone ever, by fussing in front of the mirror, gotten taller by even an inch? All this time and money wasted on fashion – do you really think it makes that much of a difference?

Instead of obsessing over fashion, go out into the fields and really look at the wildflowers. They never get ready or go shopping, but have you ever seen colors and designs quite like theirs? The ten best-dressed people in the country look shabby next to them.
If God pays so much attention to how beautiful wildflowers look – most of which are never even seen – don't you think he'll pay attention to you, be proud of you, and do his absolute best for you?

What I'm trying to get you to do here is to chill out, to not be so obsessed with getting stuff, so you can actually respond to all the amazing things God is giving you. People who don't know God and how he works stress out over these things, but you know both God and how he works.
Steep your life in God's reality, God's initiatives, and God's provisions. Don't worry about missing out. You'll find that all your everyday human concerns will totally be met.

Give your complete attention to what God is doing right now, and don't get all worked up about what may or may not happen tomorrow. God will help you deal with whatever hard things come up when the time actually comes.

title: Stop Playing Referee (Sermon on the Mount, Finale)
paragraphs: § A Simple Guide for Behavior

Alright, listen up: Don't be that person who constantly picks on others, jumping all over their failures or criticizing every little fault – unless you're cool with getting the exact same treatment back. Because, seriously, that critical attitude you're putting out? It's totally going to boomerang right back at you.

It's super easy to notice a tiny smudge on your friend's face but completely miss the ugly, judgmental look on your own. How can you even think about saying, "Hey, let me help you with that," when your own expression is all twisted up with contempt?

It's like you're putting on a whole show, acting all 'holier-than-thou' instead of just focusing on living your own part. Just wipe that nasty sneer off your own face first, and *then* maybe you'll actually be in a good place to genuinely offer a washcloth to your neighbor.

Also, don't be disrespectful or casual with things that are sacred, things that are about God. Joking around or being silly about them doesn't honor God at all. Don't try to reduce deep, holy mysteries to simple, catchy slogans. When you try too hard to make it 'relevant' or 'cute,' you're just being cute, and you're inviting disrespect for what's holy.
And when it comes to God, don't try to bargain with Him. Just be direct. Ask for what you need. This isn't some weird game of cat-and-mouse or hide-and-seek we're playing.

Think about it: If your kid asks for bread, would you trick them by giving them sawdust? If they ask for fish, would you scare them by putting a live snake on their plate? Even if you're not the best person ever, you wouldn't even think of doing something like that. You're at least decent to your own children.
So, don't you think the God who created you out of pure love will be even *better* and more generous than you are?

Here's a super simple, common-sense guide for how to act: Ask yourself what you want people to do for you, then be the one to take the initiative and do that for them. Seriously, if you add up everything in God's Law and what the Prophets taught, this is basically the main takeaway.
§ Being and Doing

Don't go looking for shortcuts to God. The world is full of these 'surefire, easygoing' formulas for a successful life that promise you can do it in your spare time. Don't fall for that stuff, even though tons of people do.
The real path to life – to God! – is active and requires your full attention. It's not a walk in the park.

Be really careful of those fake preachers who always have a big smile, dripping with practiced sincerity. Chances are, they're just out to rip you off in some way or another. Don't be impressed by their charisma; look for their actual character. Who these preachers *are* is the main thing, not just what they say.
A genuine leader will never try to mess with your emotions or your wallet. These 'diseased trees' with their 'bad apples' are going to be chopped down and burned.
Just knowing the right password – like saying "Master, Master" – isn't going to get you anywhere with me. What's really required is serious obedience – actually *doing* what my Father wants.

I can picture it now: at the Final Judgment, thousands will strut up to me, saying, "Master, we preached your Message, we totally bashed demons, and our super-spiritual projects had everyone talking!" And do you know what I'm going to say?
"You totally missed the boat. All you did was use me to make yourselves look important. You don't impress me one bit. Get out of here."

These words I'm speaking to you aren't just little extras for your life, like home improvements to your standard of living. They are foundational words, words to build your whole life on. If you actually work these words into your life, you're like a smart carpenter who built his house on solid rock.
Rain poured down, the river flooded, a tornado hit – but nothing moved that house. It was fixed firmly to the rock.

But if you just use my words in Bible studies and don't actually put them into practice in your life, you're like a stupid carpenter who built his house on the sandy beach. When a storm rolled in and the waves came up, it just collapsed like a house of cards.
When Jesus finished speaking, the crowd totally burst into applause. They had never heard teaching like this before.
It was super clear that he was actually living everything he was saying – what a huge contrast to their usual religion teachers! This was seriously the best teaching they had ever heard.
